history.origins: The game originated in Nepal, where it is known as Dhumbal or Jhyap (Jhyap is Nepali slang meaning intoxicated or high). Around the beginning of the 21st century it became popular in Israel under the name Yaniv among young players and Israeli backpackers, both at home and when travelling; the backpacker community often attributes the Israeli version to two travellers named Yaniv and Asaf who are said to have devised it to pass time on long bus and train journeys in East Asia or South America. It has since spread to other countries, including the Netherlands where a variant is called Kluft, and is now an iconic social card game in Israel.
timeline: Early 21st century: Became popular in Israel under the name Yaniv; originated in Nepal as Dhumbal/Jhyap.
history.cultural: Israel's iconic social card game; strongly associated with backpacker culture and youth play.
history.evolution: Spread internationally through Israeli backpacker culture and travel; regional variants (e.g. Kluft in the Netherlands) adopted local names and minor rule differences.
